concepts.title: Sources of Information About the Earth's Interior
concepts.definition: Direct sources of the earth's interior are mining and drilling projects like the Kola superdeep borehole, while indirect sources include seismic waves, meteorites, gravitation, magnetic field and density studies that reveal a layered interior.
concepts.key_idea: Seismic waves behave differently in each layer, so their speed and direction reveal the crust, mantle and core and the discontinuities between them.

concepts.title: Layers of the Earth: Crust, Mantle, Core and Rocks
concepts.definition: The earth divides into the thin crust of sial and sima, the mantle with upper and lower parts separated by the Moho and Repetti discontinuities, and the core of nickel and iron divided by the Gutenberg discontinuity, made of rocks of igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic types in the crust.
concepts.key_idea: The asthenosphere in the upper mantle is the source of magma, and the core's liquid outer part and solid inner part explain the shadow zones of seismic waves.

concepts.title: Earthquakes, Volcanoes and Their Interior Links
concepts.definition: Earthquakes release energy as seismic waves along faults, volcanoes erupt magma from the asthenosphere, and both phenomena connect to the layered interior and moving plates, with epicentre, focus and intensity scales describing their occurrence.
concepts.key_idea: Study of the interior explains why earthquakes cluster at plate boundaries and why volcanic rocks like basalt reveal mantle material at the surface.
